hints: Focus on the Hess cycle idea that reaction enthalpy is products minus reactants using formation enthalpies.
Remember to multiply each formation value by its balancing number, so 3 lots of $\text{VCl}_2$ and 2 lots of $\text{VCl}_3$, and note that $\text{V(s)}$ as an element is zero.
Work out $2(-573) - 3(-452)$ carefully with the signs and see whether the overall result is endothermic or exothermic.
walkthrough:
**Recall the formation enthalpy rule**

Think of formation enthalpies as building compounds from elements. The reaction enthalpy is what you make minus what you break.

$$\Delta H_r^\ominus = \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta H_f^\ominus(\text{reactants})$$

**Write out products and reactants**

Products are $2\text{VCl}_3 + \text{V}$. Reactants are $3\text{VCl}_2$. Do not forget the moles in front.

$$\text{products} = 2 \times (-573) + 0$$
$$\text{reactants} = 3 \times (-452)$$

**Do the arithmetic and decide the sign**

Products total is $-1146 \text{ kJ}$. Reactants total is $-1356 \text{ kJ}$. Subtracting gives a positive value.

$$\Delta H_r^\ominus = -1146 - (-1356) = +210 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$$

**Conclude the answer**

A positive value means the disproportionation is endothermic. That matches +210 kJ per equation as written.

options.A: Incorrect. This is the same magnitude but the wrong sign. It comes from doing reactants minus products instead of products minus reactants.
options.B: Incorrect. This is simply $(-573) - (-452) = -121$. It forgets to multiply by the 3 and 2 in the balanced equation, a very common trap.
options.C: Incorrect. This is the reverse of option B, $(-452) - (-573) = +121$. It also ignores the balancing numbers 3 and 2.
options.D: Correct. Using $\Delta H_r = \sum \Delta H_f(\text{products}) - \sum \Delta H_f(\text{reactants})$ gives $2(-573) + 0 - 3(-452) = -1146 + 1356 = +210 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
